newsitem.title: USA: Zions wants direct sub to deal muni bonds.
newsitem.headline: Zions wants direct sub to deal muni bonds.

text.p: Zions First National Bank, a unit of Zions Bancorp is seeking permission to deal in municipal bonds through a direct operating subsidiary, U.S. Office of the Comptroller said on Wednesday.

Under a controversial rule approved by the comptroller's office last November, national banks can recieve permission to conduct non-banking activities that are closely related to banking through direct subsidiaries.
Bank subsidiaries can underwrite general obligation muni bonds, but previously have been required to underwrite municipal revenue bonds through separate affiliates.

The Zions application is the second under the new OCC rule. Last month, Nationsbank was the first to file an application under the new rule. It sought permission to establish real estate leasing and development businesses.
Although banks can underwrite revenue bonds through affiliates, many have complained that the requirement to establish a separate unit was too costly.

Zions said in its application that it already underwrites and deals in general obligation muni bonds. The bank wants to conduct the new activity through one of its existing subsidiaries that currently provides brokerage and investment advisory services relating to securities and investment products.
Zions officials were not imemdiately available for comment.
OCC said it would publish Zions' request in the Federal Register this week and accept comments for 30 days before making a decision.
